note: What a server sends to put a turret on the field. A server sends it only inside EnterSight, and the channel and delivery given here are those of the message carrying it. The header names the unit this is about.

fields.name: turret
fields.note: The name the turret answers to, so later messages can name it.

fields.name: node
fields.note: Which network node the object belongs to, in a field of its own.

fields.name: name
fields.note: What this turret is called, so a client can tell one from another. Written out in full and padded with zero bytes to the width above.

revisions.note: A client matches name exactly against the map's turrets. With no match it only removes any object holding the id; a matched turret missing or dead is rebuilt before it takes the id.

bits.name: targetable
bits.note: It has no effect: a turret's targetability comes by replication.

fields.name: targetableBy
fields.note: Who can target the turret. A server writes the value replication carries for the turret: 8388608 not its own side, 16777216 not the other side, 25165824 nobody, 33554432 everyone, anything else both sides. A client takes the turret's targetability from replication alone.
